ex.en: Do you remember our first meeting?
Today's get-together was really fun.
I hope I meet someone good.

note: Counter: 마리 (고양이 두 마리).

ex.s: 우리 집 고양이는 하루 종일 자요.
ex.en: Our cat sleeps all day.
Have you ever had a cat?
There's a cat sitting in front of the café.
Did you install this app?
A technician is coming tomorrow to install the AC.
I need to install a program on my work computer.

note: Spoken exclamation; also written 우와.

ex.en: Wow, the view is really nice!
Wow, this is so delicious.
Wow, it's already twelve?
It's prettier in person than in the photo.
If you actually go, it's closer than you think.
Have you actually met that actor?

note: Often paired with -(으)ㄹ 거예요.

ex.en: It'll probably rain tomorrow.

ex.s: 민호 씨는 아마 집에 있을 거예요.
ex.en: Minho is probably at home.

ex.s: 아마 열 시쯤 도착할 것 같아요.
ex.en: I'll probably arrive around ten.

note: 수술하다 = to operate; 수술(을) 받다 = to have surgery.

ex.en: My father is having surgery next week.
The surgery went well.
You need to rest a few days after surgery.

note: Adverb 엄청 (really, super) is very common in speech.

ex.en: It's the weekend, so there are tons of people.
That place's pizza is enormous.

ex.s: 이번 달 전기 요금이 엄청나게 나왔어요.
ex.en: This month's electric bill came out huge.
You made it all yourself? That's amazing!
You work out every day? That's impressive.
That person's singing is impressive.
This summer is really hot.
What's your goal for this year?
My daughter starts elementary school this year.

note: Used with 에: 헬스장에 가입하다.

ex.en: If you sign up for this site, you get a discount.
I joined a neighborhood soccer group.
I'd like to sign up for insurance.
I'll ask a staff member.
The staff at that restaurant are all friendly.
Our company has twenty employees.
It's quite far from here to the airport.
You speak Korean pretty well.
It's fairly cold today.

note: Used for adults; for children use 어리다.

ex.en: Our teacher is younger than I thought.
Travel a lot while you're young.
There are many young people in this neighborhood.
Did you bring an umbrella?
Make sure you pack your passport.
Even if you're busy, make sure you eat properly.
I'll handle this.
We'll process your refund by today.

ex.s: 이메일이 너무 많아서 다 처리 못 했어요.
ex.en: I had too many emails to get through them all.

note: Honorific of 형; used by males, also for older male friends.

ex.en: Hey, big brother, long time no see.
I'm going to my older brother's place for dinner.
I should give my older brother a call.
I went for a walk in the woods on the weekend.
The air in the forest is really nice.
If you take this path, you'll reach a forest.
I signed up for a city tour tomorrow.
What time does the tour start?
The guided tour was really fun.

note: 건강하다 = to be healthy.

ex.en: Take care of your health.
I started exercising lately for my health.
How is your grandmother's health?
The baby is sleeping right now.
What's the baby's name?
Does the restaurant have a high chair?
I'll do the rest tomorrow.
Please wrap up the rest of the food.

ex.s: 오만 원 내고 나머지는 카드로 할게요.
ex.en: I'll pay 50,000 won and put the rest on card.
The whole family gets together on holidays.
What time and where are we meeting?
A lot of people gathered in the park.

note: Uses native numbers: 한 마리, 두 마리, 세 마리.

ex.en: I have two dogs.
One whole chicken, please.
How many cats do you have?
I was late, so I ran to the station.
I run in the park every morning.
I'm so nervous my heart is pounding.
I laughed a lot watching that movie.
I'm taking the picture, smile!
The baby smiles at her mom.
Don't lose hope.

ex.s: 의사 선생님 말씀 듣고 희망이 생겼어요.
ex.en: I felt hopeful after hearing what the doctor said.
If you have any requests, let me know.

note: 기대하다 = to look forward to; 기대돼요 = I'm excited.

ex.en: I'm so excited about the trip.
That restaurant was worse than I expected.
Don't get your hopes up too much.
I'll look into hotel prices.
I'm looking for a new place these days.
You cut your hair, so I didn't recognize you.

note: Private after-school institute: 영어 학원, 피아노 학원.

ex.en: My son goes to a math academy in the evening.
I'm taking classes at a cooking school these days.
I'll call you after my class.

note: Used in comparisons: 훨씬 더, 훨씬 싸요.

ex.en: The subway is much faster than a taxi.
I feel much better after taking the medicine.
It's way cheaper here than over there.

note: Work context: 업무 시간 = business hours.

ex.en: I have way too much work today.

ex.s: 업무 시간은 아홉 시부터 여섯 시까지예요.
ex.en: Business hours are from nine to six.
I'm still getting used to my new duties.
Could you throw me the ball?
I threw a toy to the dog.
Don't throw trash just anywhere.

note: Usually 덕분에; 덕분에요 = thanks to you.

ex.en: Thanks to your help, we finished quickly.
Thanks to my friend, I didn't get lost.
Thanks to the weather, the trip was fun.
Are you a member, by any chance?

ex.s: 회원 가입하면 커피 한 잔 무료예요.
ex.en: If you sign up as a member, you get a free coffee.
Our club has ten members.

note: Adverb 분명히 = definitely, clearly.

ex.en: I clearly told you.
I'm sure I left the keys here.
That person's answer wasn't clear.
I want to learn the basics again.
How much is the base fare?
Saying hello is basic manners.

en: main character, lead; star of occasion

ex.en: Who's the lead in this drama?
The lead's acting was really good.
Today's star is Ji-woo!

note: Near-synonym of 아래.

ex.en: The keys were under the sofa.
We waited out the rain under the bridge for a bit.
Please write your name below the photo.
I'm going to tidy my room this weekend.
Please organize the meeting notes.
I feel good after organizing my closet.

note: 인기가 많다 / 인기 있다 = to be popular.

ex.en: This is our most popular dish.

ex.s: 요즘 그 노래 인기 진짜 많아요.
ex.en: That song is really popular these days.
Minho was popular at school.
What's causing the headache?
We still don't know what caused the breakdown.
Stress might be the cause.

note: 효과가 있다 = to work, be effective.

ex.en: Does this medicine work?
I can already see the results of working out.
The sale had a pretty big effect.

note: Slightly formal; 아이 / 애 is more casual.

ex.en: How much is the children's fare?
This park has a children's playground.
Do you have a kids' menu too?

note: 구매하다 = to buy (more formal than 사다).

ex.en: It's cheaper if you buy it online.

ex.s: 구매 후 7일 안에 교환할 수 있어요.
ex.en: You can exchange it within 7 days of purchase.
Check your purchase history in the app.
My uncle works at a car factory.
I went on a factory tour.
These snacks came straight from the factory.

note: ㅂ-irregular: 귀여워요.

ex.en: The puppy is so cute!
This cup is really cute.
My nephew's smile is really cute.
I grew up in the countryside.
Kids grow up really fast.
Your hair has grown a lot.
Is there a pharmacy around here?
I eat lunch near my office.
Call me if you're in the area.
My grades went up a lot this semester.
When do report cards come out?
Health matters more than grades.

note: Casual spoken intensifier; standard adverb is 완전히.

ex.en: This movie is totally fun.
I'm completely exhausted today.
That shop is super cheap.
Don't worry, it's nothing serious.
Why do you look so serious?
The traffic in Seoul is bad.
Please change the channel.
I watch cooking channels a lot these days.
Please subscribe to my YouTube channel.
Have you been to the new café?
I bought a new phone.
The new employee is really kind.

note: Used with 에 or 을/를: 계획에 반대하다.

ex.en: My parents are against me studying abroad.
I disagree with that opinion.
Is anyone against it?
It's impossible to finish by today.
Reservations aren't possible on weekends.
Nothing is impossible.

note: 노력하다 = to try hard, make an effort.

ex.en: The results matched the effort I put in.
I'll try even harder.
I put a lot of effort into studying Korean.
You need to protect your skin from UV rays.
I bought a case to protect my phone.
Protecting the kids is the most important thing.

note: 그만하다 = to stop; 그만두다 = to quit.

ex.en: Stop crying now.
I'll stop eating, I'm full.
Let's call it a night.

note: Slightly more emphatic or written than 더.

ex.en: It got even colder because of the rain.
I'll work even harder from now on.
It's even prettier at night.

note: 식사하다 = to eat; 식사하셨어요? is a polite greeting.

ex.en: Have you had lunch?
Enjoy your meal.
Take the medicine after meals.
I teach English at a high school.

ex.s: 이 단어 뜻 좀 가르쳐 주세요.
ex.en: Please tell me what this word means.
My dad taught me how to swim.
Winter in Korea is really cold.

ex.s: 이번 겨울에 스키 타러 갈 거예요.
ex.en: I'm going skiing this winter.
I haven't taken out my winter clothes yet.

note: ㄷ-irregular: 깨달아요, 깨달았어요.

ex.s: 집에 와서 지갑이 없는 걸 깨달았어요.
ex.en: I got home and realized my wallet was gone.

ex.s: 아프고 나서 건강이 중요한 걸 깨달았어요.
ex.en: After being sick, I realized how important health is.
I didn't realize it was a mistake at the time.

ex.s: 이 경험은 평생 못 잊을 거예요.
ex.en: I'll never forget this experience.
My grandmother lived in this village all her life.
My grandfather never smoked in his whole life.
Please put the leftover side dishes in a container.
I put it in my shopping cart.
I'll put a little more rice in the bowl.

note: Opposite of 켜다. Conjugates 꺼요.

ex.en: Please turn off the lights when you leave.
Please turn off your phone in the theater.
Is it okay if I turn off the AC?
The weather is getting colder and colder.
Korean is getting more and more fun.
The child looks more and more like his dad.
I applied to that company.
I'm going to try applying for a scholarship.
My company covers transportation costs.

note: Used with 에: 의견에 동의하다.

ex.en: I agree with that too.
You have to agree to the terms to sign up.
The whole family agreed to the move.
What are the rules of this game?
The dorm rules are a bit strict.
Please follow the rules.

note: Synonym of 항상.

ex.en: I'm always grateful to you.
That friend is always late.
I always have bread for breakfast.

note: 담당자 = the person in charge.

ex.en: I'm in charge of this project.
My husband is in charge of cooking at home.
Is the person in charge here?
My schedule is really busy this week.
Did you plan the whole trip itinerary?
Let me know if the schedule changes.

note: 가게 주인 = shop owner; 집주인 = landlord.

ex.en: Whose bag is this?
The shop owner was really kind.
Did you call the landlord?

ex.s: 외국인도 이 카드 만들 수 있어요?
ex.en: Can foreigners get this card too?
A lot of foreigners live in this neighborhood.

ex.s: 우리 식당에는 외국인 손님이 많이 와요.
ex.en: Lots of foreign customers come to our restaurant.
I'll go fill up my water bottle.
I filled up the tank at the gas station.
Please fill in the blanks.
This video is really funny.
I'll film a video of the baby and send it.
I followed along with a cooking video.

note: Often 가득하다 or 가득 차다.

ex.en: The subway is packed with people.
Please fill it all the way with water.
The fridge is full of food.
We're having a party at my place on Friday.
Who did you invite to the birthday party?
Was the office party fun yesterday?

note: Usually a high-rise complex unit, often owned.

ex.en: I live on the tenth floor of an apartment building.

ex.s: 이 근처 아파트 가격이 많이 올랐어요.
ex.en: Apartment prices around here have gone up a lot.
There's a playground in front of the apartment.

note: 상처(를) 받다 = to get hurt (feelings).

ex.en: I got a cut on my hand.
Put a bandage on the cut.
I was hurt by what they said.

note: More formal than 길.

ex.en: The roads are slippery because of the rain.
This road is always jammed.
Be careful crossing the road.
What's the title of that song?
Please make sure to add a subject line to the email.
I can't remember the book's title.

en: to be a waste, too good to lose
note: ㅂ-irregular: 아까워요. Said when something feels wasted.

ex.en: It's a waste to leave food.
That movie was a waste of money.

ex.s: 한 골 차이로 져서 너무 아까워요.
ex.en: It's such a shame we lost by one goal.

note: ㅅ-irregular: 저어요, 저었어요.

ex.s: 커피에 설탕 넣고 잘 저어 주세요.
ex.en: Add sugar to the coffee and stir it well.
Keep stirring so the sauce doesn't burn.
When I asked, he shook his head.

note: 대중교통 = public transportation.

ex.en: Public transportation in Seoul is really convenient.
Traffic is heavy during rush hour.
I need to top up my transit card.

note: Passive of 부르다.

ex.en: I was often called by a nickname as a kid.
What is this food called in Korea?
My name was called at the hospital.
The meeting went on until evening.
This road leads all the way to the sea.
The hot weather is continuing.
I'm going to Seoul via Tokyo.
This document has to go through the team leader.
This bus goes by City Hall.

note: 피해를 주다 = to bother or harm others.

ex.en: You shouldn't cause trouble for the neighbors.
I'll keep quiet so I don't bother anyone.
The typhoon caused a lot of damage.
We did a fun experiment in science class.
I'm experimenting with a new recipe.
The experiment results come out tomorrow.

note: 발전하다 = to develop, improve.

ex.en: Your Korean has really improved.
This city is developing really fast.
Life got easier thanks to advances in technology.
That restaurant has good reviews.
I have a performance review next week.
This movie's reviews aren't great.
Change the language in your phone's settings.
Did you set the alarm?
Please show me how to set it up.

ex.s: 블로그 후기 보고 이 식당에 왔어요.
ex.en: I came to this restaurant after reading blog reviews.
I'm writing a travel blog these days.
I posted the photos on my blog.

note: Korean men have mandatory service; 군대 가다 = enlist.

ex.en: My older brother goes into the army next month.
I made a lot of friends in the military.
I went back to school after the army.

note: Slightly literary; 남자아이 is more common in speech.

ex.en: That boy showed me the way.
This novel is the story of a boy.
As a boy, all I did was play soccer.

note: 변경하다 = to change (plans, settings).

ex.en: Can I change my reservation?
Contact me if there's a schedule change.
I need to change my password.

note: Common: 꿈을 이루다 = to make a dream come true.

ex.en: I finally achieved my dream.
I want to achieve all my goals this year.
I hope your wish comes true!
